01.r: The chief priests as a known body.

02.r: Moves the story to the priests' response.

03.r: The leading priests of the temple.
03.n: The register's rendering is 'high priest', but Abbott-Smith gives the plural as 'chief priests, including ex-high-priests and members of high-priestly families'. Since only one man held the high priesthood at a time, this study uses 'chief priests' for the plural.

06.r: The silver coins brought back to the priests.
06.n: Abbott-Smith gives the word's proper sense as 'a piece of silver'; the plural here means silver coins. Register: silver.

09.n: An impersonal verb, 'it is permitted, lawful'; Abbott-Smith lists this verse among its uses with an infinitive.

10.r: To add the coins to the temple funds.
10.n: The verb Mark uses of people putting money into the treasury (Mark 12:41).

14.r: The temple treasury that held offerings dedicated to God.
14.n: Not the usual word for treasury (γαζοφυλάκιον, as in Mark 12:41) but κορβανᾶς; our brief gives Abbott-Smith's entry for the related κορβάν, 'an offering, a gift offered to God' (Mark 7:11), which points to this word. This study renders it 'Corban treasury' to keep that link and to keep the two words apart. Only the DRC keeps the word itself, 'corbona'.

15.r: Gives the reason the money is barred.
15.n: Abbott-Smith's causal sense, 'since, because', with this verse listed.

16.r: The money paid for handing Jesus over to death.
16.n: Abbott-Smith gives the word's root sense as 'a valuing', then 'a price paid or received', citing this verse's phrase 'price of blood'. In the Septuagint it stands for עֵרֶךְ, the word this study renders 'valuation'.

17.r: Blood stands for a life taken.
